1. How this document should be used
blocks.normalizedText: The canonical Closy garment is a structured, simulation-ready garment consisting of sewing panels, seams, semantic parts, material properties and body correspondence. 3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: A user supplies photographs or a short guided capture of a real garment. Closy reconstructs an editable, simulation-ready digital garment, fits it to the user's avatar, preserves the garment's visible design and material character, predicts plausible hidden structure, and displays it at a quality appropriate to the device.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: This is not merely “turn an image into a mesh.” A successful garment must support:

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 1. Identity — it should still look like the uploaded garment.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 2. Structure — sleeves, collar, waist, panels, openings and seams should be represented meaningfully.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 3. Fit — it should align to a body of known shape and measurements.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 4. Simulation — it should drape and move rather than behave like a rigid statue.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 5. Editability — dimensions, fit, material and appearance should be adjustable.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 6. Layering — it should eventually coexist with underwear, shirts, jackets and accessories.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 7. Animation — it should follow a posed or animated avatar.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 8. Scalability — it should have desktop, mobile and high-detail render derivatives.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 9. Traceability — the system should know which regions are observed, inferred or generated.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: 10. Safety and privacy — user photographs and body estimates must be handled as sensitive personal data.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
3. Product mission
blocks.normalizedText: A generated object that resembles a shirt in one turntable render but has fused sleeves, no neck opening, unusable UVs and no body correspondence does not satisfy this mission.

4.1 Generic 3D generation is not garment reconstruction
blocks.normalizedText: A generic image-to-3D model tries to produce a visually plausible surface. Garment reconstruction must infer hidden panels, openings, seams, body clearance and physical behaviour.

4. What must not be conflated
4.2 Retopology is not semantic garment topology
blocks.normalizedText: A clean triangle or quad mesh can still be structurally wrong. Closy needs to know that an edge is a cuff, an armhole, a waistband or one side of a stitched seam.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
4. What must not be conflated
4.3 UV unwrapping is not sewing-pattern recovery
blocks.normalizedText: A generic UV atlas cuts a surface into charts for texturing. A sewing pattern represents how fabric was cut and stitched. The two can overlap, but they are not interchangeable.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration

4. What must not be conflated
4.4 Rigging is not cloth simulation
blocks.normalizedText: Skinning a shirt to the body skeleton can provide a cheap fallback preview, but it will not produce realistic drape, lag, folding or collision behaviour.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration

4.5 Nanite-style rendering is not simulation

4. What must not be conflated
4.5 Nanite-style rendering is not simulation
blocks.normalizedText: Clustered virtual geometry determines what detail should be rendered and streamed. It does not decide how fabric stretches, bends, collides or settles.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
4. What must not be conflated
4.6 Appearance accuracy is not physical accuracy
blocks.normalizedText: A generated normal map may imitate folds without giving the garment correct mass, bending stiffness, stretch or friction.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration

4.7 A high-resolution mesh is not automatically a high-quality asset
blocks.normalizedText: Millions of triangles can encode noise, self-intersections and hallucinated details. Quality must be measured by structure, fidelity, deformation and runtime behaviour, not triangle count alone.

4. What must not be conflated
4.1 Generic 3D generation is not garment reconstruction
requirements.normalizedText: A generic image-to-3D model tries to produce a visually plausible surface. Garment reconstruction must infer hidden panels, openings, seams, body clearance and physical behaviour.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
4. What must not be conflated
4.2 Retopology is not semantic garment topology
requirements.normalizedText: A clean triangle or quad mesh can still be structurally wrong. Closy needs to know that an edge is a cuff, an armhole, a waistband or one side of a stitched seam.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
4. What must not be conflated
4.5 Nanite-style rendering is not simulation
requirements.normalizedText: Clustered virtual geometry determines what detail should be rendered and streamed. It does not decide how fabric stretches, bends, collides or settles.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
4. What must not be conflated
4.7 A high-resolution mesh is not automatically a high-quality asset
requirements.normalizedText: Millions of triangles can encode noise, self-intersections and hallucinated details. Quality must be measured by structure, fidelity, deformation and runtime behaviour, not triangle count alone.

requirements.normalizedText: These principles should survive individual model and library changes.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
5. Core design principles
5.1 Pattern-first canonical truth
requirements.normalizedText: The canonical garment should contain an explicit pattern and seam graph whenever the category supports cut-and-sew construction.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
5. Core design principles
5.2 Multiple representations, one garment
requirements.normalizedText: Closy should not force one mesh to perform every job. A garment may have:

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
5. Core design principles
5.3 The simulation mesh drives the render mesh
requirements.normalizedText: Cloth physics should run on a regular, semantically useful simulation mesh. The dense mesh follows it through a stored binding.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
5. Core design principles
5.4 Existing models are providers, not the architecture
requirements.normalizedText: Meshy, Hunyuan3D, TRELLIS and future models should sit behind adapters. Replacing a provider must not rewrite the garment package, simulation or app.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
5. Core design principles
5.5 Confidence must be spatial and explicit
requirements.normalizedText: Every reconstructed region should be marked as observed, triangulated from several views, inferred from symmetry, generated by a prior or manually corrected.

headingPath: Closy Neural Garment Foundry and ZeroOne Virtual-Geometry Integration
